memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "So Moses took his wife and sons, put them on a donkey and started back to Egypt. And he took the staff of God in his hand." - Exodus 4:20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Look at the last phrase carefully. In verse 2 it was simply "a staff." Now it is "the staff of God."

Nothing about the wood has changed. It is the same stick he had been carrying for forty years. What changed is that it was surrendered and commissioned. Once given to God, the ordinary became holy.

That is what God does with what we hand over. A kitchen becomes a place of hospitality. A car becomes a means of ministry. A salary becomes a channel of generosity. A voice becomes an instrument of encouragement. The item is the same; the ownership is different.

Notice too that Moses takes his family with him. He is walking back into the country that once wanted him dead, and he brings his wife and sons. Obedience often costs more than one person.

Whatever is in your hand today can become the staff of God. It simply has to be given to Him first.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What ordinary thing of mine could God commission for His purposes?
2. Have I counted the cost that my obedience may have for my family?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, take what is mine and make it Yours. Let the ordinary things of my life serve Your kingdom. Amen.
